text:
sara: hey team, escalated from Customer A — their streaming SSE connections to /v1/stream keep dropping after ~55-65s. They see partial tokens and clients reconnecting, sometimes duplicate outputs. They think it's our API but logs show upstream finish at the same time. Customer reports it happens behind ALB -> nginx -> app and sometimes via Cloudflare in front.

jun: thanks — any request ids or example timestamps?

sara: provided request id `req-0a1b2c3d` and curl they used: `curl -v -N https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\"` — they did `-N` to disable output buffering on client. They attached a small repro: send one prompt, stream stops mid-token after ~58s.

matt: common culprits: ALB idle timeout (default 60s), nginx proxy_read_timeout / proxy_buffering, or Cloudflare buffering. If ALB idle is 60s and nothing is sent in that window it will close. Are we sending heartbeats?

sara: customer says they didn't implement heartbeats. Their server (app) prints continuous streaming logs until done. Our access logs show a `200` upstream but downstream closed. Example from nginx access: `10.0.0.5 - - [15/Mar/2026:12:13:41 +0000] \"GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1\" 200 0 \"-\" \"curl/7.68.0\" \"req-0a1b2c3d\"` — note body size 0 in nginx log because chunked streaming.

ricardo: can we get the nginx conf for the proxy in front of the app? Common settings to check: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_cache off; proxy_set_header Connection \"keep-alive\"; proxy_read_timeout 300s; proxy_send_timeout 300s;` Also `X-Accel-Buffering: no` header from app helps.

ops-bot: Incident note created: INC-20260315-138. Tagging eng-runtime.

katie: customer also on Cloudflare? if CF in front, CF will buffer responses for some configurations (Workers, page rules). Need `Cloudflare > Origin > Disable Response Buffering` options or use `chunked` + early bytes. CF sometimes waits for first 512 bytes.

jun: repro steps we ran locally:
```
# start simple server that streams SSE every 15s
python -m http.server 8000 &
# (we used a local python SSE app that flushes every event)
# curl with no-buffer to simulate client
curl -v -N http://localhost:8000/stream
```
We then put nginx as reverse proxy with default config and saw disconnects at ~60s. After setting `proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 180;` the connection stayed open.

matt: also check ALB/NLB: ALB has idle timeout (default 60s) which closes if no data at the TCP level. If our runtime pauses token emission >60s (e.g., long generation or batching), ALB can close. Options: increase ALB idle timeout (up to 4000s), ensure runtime emits periodic SSE comment heartbeats (`: heartbeat\n\n`) or chunked keepalives.

ricardo: for Envoy front-proxy, check `stream_idle_timeout` and `idle_timeout` on cluster / listener. For HTTP/2 upstream, Envoy may convert and cause buffering; ensure `upstream_http_protocol_options` permits `allow_metadata`? (we used a specific flag in our k8s overlay).

katie: billing note — customer concerned about being billed for partial responses. We bill per-token consumed by our runtime; if client reconnects and requests re-stream the same prompt, they may incur retries. We should explain deduping options (idempotency tokens) and advise customers to implement event reconcilers on client side.

jun: proposed mitigation checklist to send to customer: 
1) Add SSE heartbeats from the app: send `: \n\n` or a single-space comment every 15s.
2) Configure nginx: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection \"keep-alive\"; proxy_read_timeout 300s;` and ensure `X-Accel-Buffering: no` header from app.
3) If ALB in path: increase ALB idle timeout > generation max (or to 300s) or put the runtime behind a TCP-level NLB.
4) If Cloudflare: set `Origin Response Buffering` off or use `chunked` flush early bytes.
5) For Envoy: set `stream_idle_timeout` to a higher value and confirm HTTP/1.1 upgrade/streaming toggles.

sara: customer asked for an example nginx snippet and curl repro they can run. Sharing below.

matt: paste this snippet: 
```
# nginx location /v1/stream
location /v1/stream {
  proxy_pass http://upstream_app;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "";
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_cache off;
  proxy_read_timeout 300s;
  proxy_send_timeout 300s;
  proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
}
# app should send header: X-Accel-Buffering: no
```

jun: and example app-side heartbeat for SSE (node):
```
res.writeHead(200, {
  'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream',
  'Cache-Control': 'no-cache',
  'Connection': 'keep-alive',
  'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no'
});
setInterval(() => res.write(': heartbeat\n\n'), 15000);
// stream tokens as they arrive: res.write(`data: ${token}\n\n`)
```

ricardo: customer ran the nginx change and ALB bump to 180s in staging and reported streaming stable. They still saw one case where client reconnected because their client library buffered and didn't flush — recommended they use `EventSource` in browser or curl `-N`.

katie: summary for Customer A to send: explain root cause (proxy idle / buffering closing connection when no bytes sent for ~60s), provide nginx snippet + heartbeat example, ALB guidance, Cloudflare notes, and note potential billing implications + idempotency suggestions. Ask if they'd like us to validate their stack config via a short screen-share.

sara: thanks all — I'll send the mitigation checklist and ask if they want a config review. Closing thread after customer ack.
